ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two identical objects A, B are stacked together and placed on a rough horizontal tabletop, a light rope connected to object B passes over a fixed pulley and is connected to an empty box C, inside the box there is a small ball in contact with the right side of the inner wall of the box, and the entire system is in a stationary state. It is known that the masses of A and B are both m, the mass of C is M, the mass of the small ball is $m_0$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between object B and the tabletop is $\mu $, the acceleration due to gravity is g, and pulley friction and air resistance are neglected. Which of the following statements is correct ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The magnitude of the frictional force exerted on the tabletop by the object is $(M+m_{0})g$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, object A is stacked on object B, and B is placed on a rough horizontal tabletop; a light rope is connected to the right side of B, and the rope goes horizontally to the right, passes over the fixed pulley at the edge of the table, then goes vertically downward, suspending box C; inside box C there is a small ball, and the small ball is in contact with the right side wall inside the box; the entire device is in a stationary state. Then reason: Treat box C and the small ball as a whole. Since the system is stationary, the forces in the vertical direction are balanced. The whole is subjected to the upward rope tension T, and the downward weight is (M+m0)g, so T=(M+m0)g. The light rope and fixed pulley are ideal, so the magnitude of the horizontal pulling force exerted by the other end of the rope on B is also T. Treat A and B as a whole; in the horizontal direction they are stationary, so the static friction force exerted by the tabletop on B must balance the pull of the rope, with magnitude T. By Newton's third law, the magnitude of the frictional force exerted on the tabletop by the object is also equal to T. Final answer: The magnitude of the frictional force exerted on the tabletop by the object is (M+m0)g.
